exampleAnswers.title: Describing Properties of the Sine Function

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=\sin{x}?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.

  1. The function intersects the $x$-axis at $x=n\pi.$
  2. The function has minimum values at $x=-\dfrac{\pi}{2}+n\pi.$
  3. The range of the function is $y\in[-2\pi,2\pi].$
question.explanation:
Let's plot the graph of $y=\sin{x}.$

Let's go through each statement.

  • Statement I is true. The zeros occur at $x=0, \pm \pi, \pm 2\pi,\ldots,$ which can be written as $x=n\pi.$

  • Statement II is false. The function has a minimum at $x=-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\ldots,$ and the period is $2\pi.$ Therefore, the minimum values occur at $-\dfrac{\pi}{2}+2n\pi.$

  • Statement III is false. The minimum value is $-1,$ the maximum value is $1,$ and so the range is $y\in[-1,1].$

exampleAnswers.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Sine Function

question.explanation:
The period of $y = \sin x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have \[ \sin{x} = \sin(x+2n\pi). \]

Substituting $n=-7$ into the right-hand-side gives \begin{align*} \sin{x} = \sin(x-14\pi). \end{align*}

Therefore, if $\sin{x} = -\dfrac{\sqrt 3}{5},$ then $\sin(x-14\pi) = -\dfrac{\sqrt 3}{5}.$

Finally, then \begin{align} -10\sin(x-14\pi)+1 = -10\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt 3}{5}\right) + 1 = 2\sqrt 3 +1. \end{align}

example.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Sine Function

question.explanation:
The period of $y = \sin x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have \[ \sin{x} = \sin(x+2n\pi). \]

Substituting $n=-6$ into the left-hand-side gives \begin{align*} \sin{x} = \sin(x-12\pi). \end{align*}

Therefore, if $\sin{x} = -\dfrac{\sqrt 6}3,$ then $\sin(x-12\pi) = -\dfrac{\sqrt 6}3.$

Finally, we get \[ 6\sin(x-12\pi) = 6\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt 6}3\right)=-2\sqrt6. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Utilizing the Oddness Property of the Sine Function

question.explanation:
First, let's recall the graph of $y = \sin{x}.$

From the graph, we note the following:

  • The period of $\sin{x}$ is $2\pi.$

  • Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. This means that $\sin{x}$ is an odd function, and we have \[ \sin(-x) = -\sin{x}. \]

Let's now evaluate our expression:

  • Firstly, using the periodicity of $\sin{x},$ we have \begin{align*} \sin(-x - 4\pi) &= \sin(-x - 2\pi \cdot 2) \\[5pt] &= \sin(-x). \end{align*}

  • Secondly, using the oddness of $\sin{x},$ we have \begin{align*} \sin(-x) &= -\sin{x} \\[5pt] & = -0.44. \end{align*}

Therefore, $\sin(-x - 4\pi) = -0.44.$

Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. If we rotate the graph $180^\circ$ around the origin, we get the same picture. This means that $\sin{x}$ is an odd function, and we have \[ \sin(-x) = -\sin x. \]
